sections.heading: C — Lane usage, turning, changing lanes and roundabouts
sections.markdown:
## C — Lane usage, turning, changing lanes and roundabouts

FACT_ID: sec08-F01 | anchor: A01
Drive in the right-hand lane unless you are passing, or stopped vehicles, a crash or another obstacle forces you over the center line, in which case yield to oncoming traffic first. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-F02 | anchor: A01
Leaving the right lane is also allowed on roads with three or more marked lanes, on one-way streets with two or more lanes, and when signs or signals on a two-way multi-lane highway direct you left. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-F03 | anchor: A01
You may cross the center line to turn left into or out of an alley, private road or driveway. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-F04 | anchor: A01
You may leave the right lane to go around a stopped emergency vehicle once it is safe, or when road construction is near or blocking the right lane or shoulder. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-F05 | anchor: A01
On an interstate or full-access controlled freeway you must keep right, using the left lane only when congestion or weather requires it or an obstacle or hazard sits in the right lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-F06 | anchor: A01
On those freeways you may also use the left lane to move over for emergency or construction vehicles, or when no traffic is right behind or ahead of you in that lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-F07 | anchor: A01
Slow vehicles must stay in the right lane except to pass or turn left. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-F08 | anchor: A01
Weaving between lanes to speed through traffic is illegal. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-F09 | anchor: A01
Only emergency and police vehicles running lights and sirens may drive against the flow of traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-F10 | anchor: A01
Driving across median strips or through barriers is illegal, but you may turn left through a paved median cut-through when no sign forbids it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-F11 | anchor: A01
Enter and leave controlled-access roads only at designated, posted entrances and exits. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-F12 | anchor: A01
Always signal turns; hand signals for left, right and stop are now used mostly by motorcyclists, scooter and moped riders and bicyclists. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-F13 | anchor: A01
For a right turn, use the correct lane and your signal, obey signs and signals, yield to pedestrians, emergency vehicles and other traffic, and check that your left side is clear. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-F14 | anchor: A02
During a right turn, follow the curve of the curb and stay out of other lanes. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-F15 | anchor: A02
Trucks and buses need extra room to turn right. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-F16 | anchor: A02
With multiple right-turn lanes, finish the turn in the lane that matches the one you turned from, since drifting can cut off another driver and cause a crash. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-F17 | anchor: A02
For a left turn, use the correct lane and signal, obey signs and signals, and yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, emergency vehicles and other traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-F18 | anchor: A02
Keep your front wheels pointed straight until you actually begin a left turn. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-F19 | anchor: A02
With multiple left-turn lanes, end the turn in the lane that corresponds to your turn lane. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-F20 | anchor: A02
Check all approaching traffic before a left turn, looking for vehicles hidden behind or beside others, especially motorcycles, scooters and bicycles, which are easy to miss. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-F21 | anchor: A02
To move left, check behind and to your left with a head check, signal left, and move over carefully. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-F22 | anchor: A02
To move right, check behind and to your right, signal right, and move over carefully. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-F23 | anchor: A03
A roundabout is a circular intersection where traffic moves counterclockwise around a central island and entering vehicles yield to traffic coming from the left, including bicyclists and pedestrians. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F24 | anchor: A03
You leave a roundabout by turning right onto the road you want. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F25 | anchor: A03
When approaching a roundabout, use signs and pavement markings to pick the right lane, slow down, stay right of the center island, and look left as you reach the yield line. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F26 | anchor: A03
Enter a roundabout when a suitable gap appears and merge with the flow, and never turn left to enter, which puts you in front of oncoming traffic. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F27 | anchor: A03
While traveling inside a roundabout, keep right of the center island; vehicles in the roundabout hold the right of way, and you must not stop unless stopping is the only safe way to avoid a collision or other danger [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F28 | anchor: A03
If an emergency vehicle approaches while you are in a roundabout, do not stop; leave at the nearest exit, pull right and stop to let it pass. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F29 | anchor: A03
Choose your lane before entering a roundabout and avoid changing lanes inside it. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F30 | anchor: A03
Avoid passing or driving beside trucks and trailers in a roundabout, as they may need more than one lane, and do not pass other vehicles, bicycles or mopeds. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F31 | anchor: A03
Watch for pedestrians crossing as you enter or exit a roundabout. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F32 | anchor: A03
When exiting, keep a slow speed, signal your exit, and wait to accelerate until you are past the exit's pedestrian crossing; if you miss your exit, go around again. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F33 | anchor: A03
Slow down and look both ways at every railroad crossing, because a train can need a mile or more to stop and is closer and faster than it looks. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F34 | anchor: A03
Walkers, cyclists and drivers should cross tracks only at designated crossings, and walking along or stopping on tracks is illegal. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F35 | anchor: A03
The railroad advance warning sign means a crossing is ahead; with a train coming, stop no more than 50 feet and no less than 15 feet from the tracks. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-F36 | anchor: A03
Trains overhang the rails by at least three feet on each side, and cargo can stick out farther. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0049]
